title: ISTQB Foundation Mock Exam 02
description: 40-question official-style mock exam for ISTQB CTFL (English). Includes answers and explanations.

questions.text: Which statement best defines static testing?
questions.explanation: Static testing comprises reviews and static analysis of artifacts without executing the code.

questions.text: Which test principle states that testing shows the presence of defects, not their absence?
questions.explanation: Even when all executed tests pass, undiscovered defects may still exist. Testing reduces risk rather than proving defect absence.

questions.text: Decision table testing is especially useful for:

choices.text: Complex combinations of conditions and actions

questions.explanation: Decision tables capture business rules with multiple conditions and associated actions to derive thorough test cases.

questions.text: Traceability primarily enables:

choices.text: Mapping tests to requirements and back again

questions.explanation: Traceability connects requirements ↔ tests ↔ defects ↔ code to ensure coverage and impact analysis.

questions.text: Which activity is NOT part of the fundamental test process?
questions.explanation: Debugging is a development activity to locate and fix the cause of failures; it is not one of the fundamental testing activities.

questions.text: Which of the following is a structural (white‑box) technique?
questions.explanation: Decision testing (branch coverage) requires knowledge of internal logic and ensures each decision outcome is exercised.

questions.text: Equivalence partitioning is used to:

choices.text: Reduce test cases by grouping inputs with similar behavior

questions.explanation: EP groups inputs expected to be treated equivalently, allowing one representative per partition to reduce redundant tests.

questions.text: Which is a typical objective of acceptance testing?

choices.text: Assess if the system meets business needs and is ready for deployment

questions.explanation: Acceptance testing verifies fitness for use against business needs and supports the release decision.

questions.text: A common risk in test automation is that:

choices.text: Automation eliminates the need for manual exploration
Scripts become brittle when the system changes and are not maintained
Automation always runs faster than manual

questions.explanation: Without active maintenance, automation breaks as the system evolves (e.g., locator/UI changes), eroding trust in results.

questions.text: Which tool capability is MOST associated with defect management rather than test management?

choices.text: Recording, triaging, and tracking defects through workflow

questions.explanation: Defect management tools specialize in defect lifecycle workflows; test management focuses on plans, cases, runs, and traceability.

questions.text: Which activity belongs to test closure?

choices.text: Analyze lessons learned and archive testware

questions.explanation: Closure consolidates results, collects metrics, documents lessons learned, and archives testware.

questions.text: Which is a black‑box test design technique?
questions.explanation: BVA focuses on input/output boundaries without knowledge of internal code; statement/decision/condition coverage are white‑box.

questions.text: In the V‑Model, which development artifact maps to ACCEPTANCE testing on the validation side?
questions.explanation: Acceptance testing validates business requirements; system testing maps to system design; integration maps to architecture; unit to module.

questions.text: Which metric BEST indicates product quality trend during test execution?

choices.text: Defect discovery and closure rates over time

questions.explanation: Trends in defect discovery/closure inform quality and readiness decisions better than raw counts of cases or LOC.

questions.text: Given an input range 18–60 inclusive, which set provides BEST boundary tests?
questions.explanation: Best practice includes just-below, on, and just-above boundaries: 17 (below), 18 (on), 60 (on), 61 (above).

questions.text: Which activity belongs to test implementation?

choices.text: Preparing test data and test environment

questions.explanation: Implementation includes preparing procedures, data, and environment to enable execution.

questions.text: Which can be detected ONLY by dynamic testing?

choices.text: Incorrect runtime calculation due to operator precedence

questions.explanation: Runtime miscalculations require execution to observe; the others are typical static analysis findings.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a failure?

choices.text: A gap in the test plan
A human action that produces an incorrect result
An observable deviation from expected behavior during execution
A flaw in code that may cause incorrect behavior

questions.explanation: A failure is an observed incorrect behavior when the software is executed. A human action is an error; a flaw in code is a defect.

questions.text: State transition testing is best applied when:

choices.text: System behavior depends on sequences of events/state changes

questions.explanation: It models states and transitions; ideal where behavior depends on history or events.

questions.text: Which of the following is a main purpose of testing?

choices.text: To find defects and provide information about quality risks
To prove the software is perfect

questions.explanation: Testing discovers defects and provides information about product quality risks. It cannot prove perfection or remove all risks.

questions.text: Which statement best contrasts verification and validation?

choices.text: Validation checks we built the product right; verification checks we built the right product
Both occur only in system testing
Verification checks we built the product right; validation checks we built the right product

questions.explanation: Verification evaluates work‑products against specifications; validation evaluates the product against user needs and intended use.

questions.text: Risk exposure is commonly defined as:
questions.explanation: Risk exposure combines the likelihood of occurrence and the consequence (impact) to prioritize testing.

questions.text: Which option is a valid exit criterion example?

choices.text: 95% of planned tests executed with pass rate above threshold

questions.explanation: Exit criteria are measurable conditions to conclude testing (e.g., execution % and pass rate). Environment readiness is entry criterion.

questions.text: Which statement about independent testing is TRUE?

choices.text: It always finds different defects than developers
It reduces the risk of tester bias
It is performed only by external specialists
It must be scheduled after system testing

questions.explanation: Independence (testers not authoring the code) provides a fresh, unbiased perspective; it can occur at any test level.

questions.text: Which test level focuses on interactions between components?
questions.explanation: Integration testing targets interfaces and interactions among integrated components or systems.

questions.text: Which is NOT a typical goal of a review?

choices.text: Measure effectiveness of test execution progress
Find defects early in documents or code

questions.explanation: Measuring execution progress belongs to test monitoring; reviews focus on early defect detection and shared understanding.

questions.text: Which coverage metric requires that each decision outcome (True/False) be executed at least once?
questions.explanation: Decision/branch coverage ensures each branch outcome is exercised; statement ensures each statement executes at least once.

questions.text: Which is an example output from a static analysis tool?
questions.explanation: Static analysis flags code issues like unreachable code, unused variables, rule violations—without running the program.

questions.text: Which review type is the most formal, with defined roles and entry/exit criteria?
questions.explanation: Inspections are the most formal review type with roles (moderator, author, reader, recorder) and defined process checkpoints.

questions.text: Which BEST describes how risk affects test prioritization?

choices.text: Higher risk areas receive higher priority and deeper testing
Lower risk areas are always skipped

questions.explanation: Risk (probability × impact) directs more effort to areas where failures are likely and/or would be most severe.

questions.text: A typical use of a test management tool is to:

choices.text: Plan tests, manage cases and runs, and report status

questions.explanation: Test management tools handle planning, case management, execution tracking, reporting, and traceability; other tasks use other tools.

questions.text: Which is a purpose of test monitoring?

choices.text: Measure progress against the plan and report status

questions.explanation: Monitoring measures progress/metrics versus plan; control uses that information to adjust activities.

questions.text: Which is a non‑functional requirement?

choices.text: The system must store user profiles
A confirmation email must be sent after registration
Search results must be returned within two seconds
The system must allow users to reset their password

questions.explanation: Timing/performance constraints are non‑functional; the others are functional behaviors.

questions.text: Which of the following is a non‑functional test type?
questions.explanation: Usability is a non‑functional attribute. Regression is a purpose, component and acceptance are levels rather than non‑functional types.

questions.text: What is a test oracle?

choices.text: A tool that generates test data automatically
A mechanism to determine expected results for a test case

questions.explanation: A test oracle is any source that tells us the expected outcome (e.g., specs, previous version, business rules).

questions.text: Which statement about good test cases is TRUE?

choices.text: They should be clear, repeatable, and traceable to requirements
They should be vague to allow flexibility

questions.explanation: Good test cases are unambiguous, repeatable, and traceable; they include positive and negative scenarios and may be automated.

questions.text: Configuration management helps testing by ensuring:

choices.text: Testware and builds are uniquely versioned and reproducible

questions.explanation: CM ensures consistent, reproducible testing by versioning testware, environments, and builds.

questions.text: Which statement best describes confirmation testing (re‑testing)?

choices.text: Testing to ensure no unintended side effects occurred
Testing to ensure a specific previously found defect is resolved

questions.explanation: Confirmation testing verifies that the reported defect was fixed; regression testing covers potential side effects elsewhere.

questions.text: What information should an incident (defect) report include?

choices.text: Steps to reproduce and observed vs. expected results
A mandatory fix proposal by the tester

questions.explanation: A good incident report includes clear repro steps, expected/actual results, environment, severity/priority, and evidence.

questions.text: Which is a typical usability testing focus?

choices.text: User interface clarity and ease of learning

questions.explanation: Usability testing evaluates user experience attributes (learnability, efficiency, satisfaction).
